resources.string: The plan was adjusted by one of its rules.
Today\'s readiness comes from your sleep, energy, soreness and stress answers.
Lighter today: you slept less than usual, and short sleep caps how hard the session goes.
Lighter today: one of your answers was at its lowest, so the session is capped at Modified.
Lighter today: your answers together were low, so the session is capped at Light.
One step easier today: several signs of tiredness have built up over recent sessions.
You chose this level for today.
That level isn\'t open today: a safety, pain or screening limit applies.
The weight comes from your estimated best lift for this exercise.
The weight is rounded to plates and dumbbells your gym really has.
Heavier next time: you reached the target reps at the planned effort.
Same weight next time: the sets felt harder than planned.
Same weight next time, so your form can settle first.
A little lighter next time: the sets were much harder than planned.
Lighter next time: the targets were missed again, so the weight steps back to rebuild.
Aim for one more rep next time at the same weight.
The rep range grows a little before the next weight increase.
Heavier next time, starting again from the bottom of the rep range.
Same weight next time: recovery looked low on that day.
Same weight next time: there is no next step that stays within a safe weekly rise.
The increase is kept within the weekly limit for this lift.
A form tip comes with this exercise next time.
A bigger step up: this weight was clearly too light for you.
The next weight is the nearest real step your equipment allows.
The weight follows on from your last session of this exercise.
That set felt easy, so the next one is a small step heavier.
That set was hard, so the next one is a little lighter.
The weight has changed as much as it should in one session; it stays here.
An easier version is offered while your form settles.
This lift has missed its targets a few times: a lighter restart or a variation is suggested.
Fewer extra exercises today because tiredness has built up.
Your training load rose quickly this week, so the plan holds back a little.
Your days have been very similar in effort, so some variety is added.
This week\'s plan is kept under your weekly load limit.
This week is a lighter week: your body has been showing signs it needs one.
A lighter week: a few sessions are kept at Modified to let you recover.
A lighter week to finish the block before the next one starts.
A change-of-pace week between training blocks.
A lighter week is suggested; you can take it now or later.
Back from a lighter week: efforts start a little easier and build up again.
The plan moved on from a missed session; nothing is doubled up.
Welcome back: the first session after a break is a little lighter.
Easing back in after a break: weights and sets build up over the next weeks.
After a long break each exercise starts with one session to find your weight again.
Rest today: train again once you\'ve been symptom-free for a day without fever medicine.
Back after being unwell: Light first, then Modified, then normal training.
A mild head cold without fever: you can choose a Light or Modified session.
Your warm-up is built for today\'s exercises.
The warm-up is shorter today but never below its minimum.
The session was shortened to fit your time; the most important work stays.
You have extra time, so a little more useful work was added within the limits.
Short on time: a 20 to 30 minute express session is available.
An exercise was swapped for the closest match you can do today.
There\'s no close match today; other options are offered for you to choose.
No suitable swap is available for this exercise today.
Even shortened, this session needs more time than you have; the express session fits better.
Finding your weight: the next set is a little heavier.
Found it: this is your working weight for this exercise.
That was hard enough: next time starts a little lighter.
This is your working weight for now; it will go up from here.
Your health questions are all clear: standard training.
Please check with your doctor before harder exercise. Until you confirm, training stays gentle.
Moderate effort only until your doctor has said harder exercise is fine.
Stop training now. The symptom you reported needs to be checked before you train again.
Mild pain: you can go on with a lighter weight or a shorter range. Stop if it gets worse.
That exercise stops for today. Anything else you do keeps that joint gentle.
No more loading of that area today. If it doesn\'t settle, see a physiotherapist or doctor.
This area has been sore more than once: please have it checked by a physiotherapist or doctor.
A few sets were removed to stay within your safe limits.
An exercise was swapped to respect today\'s limits.
Intervals were replaced with steady work to respect today\'s limits.
Today\'s session was replaced with a Light session to stay safe.
The final safety check passed.
An exercise was left out to respect today\'s limits.
Effort targets were made easier to respect today\'s limits.
A weight was lowered to respect today\'s limits.
The cardio part was adjusted to respect today\'s limits.
Interval sessions are limited each week; this week\'s limit is reached.
A sore area is being protected: gentler exercises for it until it\'s been pain-free twice.
Your week was a little unbalanced between movements; the plan evens it out.
Extra set added.
That goes past your usual limit. Add it anyway?
That can\'t be added: it would go past the safe ceiling or load a sore area.
The reps fit your goal for this block.
Leave this many reps in reserve: stop with that many still in the tank.
Your easy cardio grows a little this week.
This week is short of the recommended activity; a brisk walk would close the gap.
This cardio machine suits today\'s session and your choices.
This interval format fits the current block.
Same version next time: keep building reps.
Ready for a harder version of this exercise next time.
An easier version next time, to keep good reps.
You can add a little weight to this exercise next time.
A little less assistance next time.
Mobility work is planned for the areas today\'s session uses.
Your starting level comes from your training experience.
Your progress moves you up a level.
After a long break you train one level lower for a few weeks.
An area you told us about is treated gently.
How hard was the whole session? A rating from 0 to 10 helps plan your next ones.
Your 12-month plan is set from your goals.
Your plan waited for you this week rather than moving on.
The training block starts again after a longer break.
This week is planned around your available days.
Fewer training days this week to fit your limits.
Days were spaced so hard sessions aren\'t back to back.
Today\'s session is ready.
Each part of the session got the best exercise for you today.
One part of the session was left out: no suitable exercise today.
Your main lifts stay the same through this block.
Some extra exercises change with the new block, for variety.
Sets are shared across the week to reach your targets safely.
Cardio is planned to support your goal.
Fast power work is left out after intervals today.
The express session keeps the most important work in 20 to 30 minutes.
This is the next session in your week.
Equipment busy: swap the exercise or do it later.
The week\'s cardio didn\'t add up as planned; it\'s adjusted.
Rest today: you reported symptoms of being unwell.
Even the lightest weight is too heavy for today\'s limit, so an easier version is used.
Your suggested goal fits your age and answers; you can change it.
Your weekly activity target is set and grows gradually.
The mix of strength and cardio suits your goal and age.
Brisk walks are planned to reach your weekly activity target.
Balance work is planned this week.
Interval sessions are now available if you\'d like them.
Your strength work keeps enough sets to protect muscle.
Your step target starts once a week of steps has been counted.
Your daily step target is set from your own first week.
Your step target goes up a little: you met it most days last week.
Your step target stays the same this week.
Your step target eases off a little for now.
Brisk walking counted toward your weekly activity.
Your weight trend is based on 7-day averages over four weeks.
Your weight has been dropping fast for three weeks. If you\'re not trying to diet or you feel unwell, please check with your doctor.
Your waist measurement is the average of your readings.
Time to measure your waist again, if you\'d like.
Your health conditions\' limits are combined; the strictest one applies.
One of your conditions needs your doctor\'s OK before harder exercise.
Please follow your care provider\'s advice instead of a training plan for now.
A limit from one of your health conditions applies today.
One condition wasn\'t recognised: please pick it again. Until then training stays gentle.
The general limits for that condition apply until you say which type it is.
Your answer about whether it\'s under control sets these limits.
No strength work today: strength days are kept apart for your health condition.
Your full warm-up was kept: your health condition needs it.
Your bone-loading block uses a gentler version today.
With your condition\'s longer warm-up, the shortest safe session is a little over 30 minutes; an easy walk is an option.
Your strength trend comes from your recent lifts.
Adding a training day with a rest day between would allow another strength day.
Your own number set the starting weight.
Your own number was too old to use directly; the weight is found again, carefully.
Welcome back. Ready when you are; today\'s plan is set.
Planning when you\'ll train makes it easier to keep going.
A calm mobility session is available for today.
Training away from the gym: exercises use only what you have with you.
Use a shorter range of movement today, keeping the stretched end.
A short bone-loading block is part of today\'s session.
